name: Rosmerta

attributes.attribute: goddess of plenty in northeastern Gaul
holds a cornucopia and sometimes the cauldron of rebirth
stands beside Mercury or beside the emperor
may be a spring goddess tied to healing
name follows a Celtic word for protection and fertility

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rosmerta is a Continental Celtic goddess. Her name can be read to mean the Great Provider, which points to her work as a goddess of plenty for the people of northeastern Gaul. Some art shows her holding a cornucopia, a horn of plenty. She also appears beside the god the Romans named Mercury, honoring their god of trade. She often stands alone, or beside a portrait of the emperor. On this basis, writers point out that her standing may have outweighed that of Mercury; the Romans held that Mercury ruled first among the gods of the Celts. Rosmerta can also be a spring goddess. Springs meant healing to the Celts, and those near river heads were bound to the fertile river goddess. The source ties her name to protection and fertility, and in some images she holds the cauldron of rebirth. Her own myth is lost, and the details of her rite are unknown.

okr.objective: Present Rosmerta as a Continental Celtic goddess of plenty whose standing may have rivaled Mercury's.
